newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon finance group may meet after U.S. election.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon finance group may meet after U.S. election.

text.p: The first meeting of a group of nations to help finance Lebanon's postwar reconstruction will not take place on October 18 as Lebanese officials said, U.S. ambassador Richard Jones said on Friday.

Jones said the consultative group might meet after the U.S. presidential election on November 5 but no date was set. He said one reason was Washington's current focus on the Israeli-Palestinian crisis.
Lebanon's acting finance minister Fouad Siniora said last week the first meeting would be on October 18.

"There is a limited amount of manpower in the U.S. administration to work on these kinds of issues that that's going to make it more difficult to have a meeting when we were hoping to have it," Jones said.
"But that does not mean that there has been a cancellation or anything like that or a postponement because the date in fact has not been set," he said.
Siniora said Lebanon will ask the group, set up in April under a ceasefire agreement that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz against Lebanon, for $5 billion over five years in donations and soft loans.
The group is being organised by the United States, which brokered the ceasefire and includes France, the European Union, Russia and other interested countries.
